title: Antipode Finder: The Opposite Side of Earth
description: Find the point exactly opposite any place on Earth with the Antipode Finder — latitude negated, longitude flipped 180 degrees. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York's antipode sits at −40.7128, 105.9940 in the Indian Ocean southwest of Australia — while Madrid's lands in the Pacific just east of New Zealand, which is why Spain and New Zealand are Earth's famous antipodal pair.
quick_answer: The Antipode Finder computes the point on Earth's surface diametrically opposite a given place — the spot you would reach by tunnelling straight through the planet's centre. Enter a place or coordinates and read its opposite: latitude negated, longitude shifted by 180 degrees, shown on the map.

Most of Spain antipodes into New Zealand waters — the rare large land-to-land pairing. Run Madrid, Wellington, Buenos Aires (China) and Quito (Sumatra) and collect Earth's four famous answers.
'Directly below us right now is…' answered with coordinates, not gestures — including the honest usual answer: open ocean.
Your antipode is roughly 12 time zones away and in the opposite season — the finder makes both facts a place instead of a slogan.
Quito, Ecuador (−0.1807, −78.4678) flips to (0.1807, 101.5322) — land, in the Sumatran jungle of Indonesia. One of the few capital-city antipodes that is not ocean.

Buenos Aires (−34.6037, −58.3816) antipodes to (34.6037, 121.6184) in eastern China near the Yellow Sea coast — the Argentina–China pairing that makes the two countries' trade routes' short way a through-Earth joke.

popular_table.note: Roughly 71% of Earth's surface is ocean, and only about 15% of land has a land antipode at all — most digs end in water. Land-to-land pairs concentrate in Spain↔New Zealand, Argentina↔China and Canada↔Antarctica's neighbourhood.

faq: Will the antipode usually be ocean?
Yes — most of the time. With oceans covering about 71% of the surface and land clustered unevenly, most points (land or sea) face water on the far side. Land antipodes are the celebrated exception.
Is the antipode the farthest place from me?
On the surface, yes — the surface distance is half Earth's circumference (about 20,015 km along the great circle), the maximum any two surface points can achieve.
The tunnel chord equals Earth's diameter (about 12,742 km through the centre) — the Earth Chord tools compute chords for shallower angles; the antipode is their limiting case.
Same antipode for my whole city?
Nearly — a city spans a few hundredths of a degree, so its antipodes span the same few hundredths on the far side. One point stands honestly for the whole town.
The North Pole's antipode is the South Pole — longitude becomes meaningless at both ends, the one place the flip formula politely breaks.
Do any two capitals antipode exactly?
Not exactly city-centre to city-centre, but the Madrid–Wellington region and Quito's Sumatran answer come close enough to run pub quizzes worldwide.
Opposite season guaranteed by geometry; the weather itself needs live data this finder does not claim to carry.
